newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
EIGHT NATIONS CHALLENGE FOR ADMIRAL'S CUP

Australia will face teams from seven, possibly eight, other nations at the 1997 Admiral's Cup to be sailed in August from Cowes, that mecca of yachting on the beautiful Isle of Wight off the south coast of England.

The Royal Ocean Racing Club announced in London this week that it had so far received challenges from Australia, Germany, Great Britain, Italy, New Zealand, Scandinavia, South Africa and the United States.
For the first time since 1975 there are three teams from the Southern Hemisphere. Australia return after missing the 1995 Cup and New Zealand are making their first appearance since 1989.
South Africa sailed the 1995 regatta after 20 years in the international sporting wilderness and are back again this year.
If the French also attend (late entries close on June 30), then there will be good reason to pop the cork on some of the product of long-running sponsor Champagne Mumm.
A fleet of nine teams would be the best line-up in years, indicating a resurgence of interest in grand prix offshore racing.

Australia finished the closest of seconds, losing to Germany by 0.25 of a point, in 1993, but missed the 1995 Cup because of the involvement of many of our major players, notably SYD FISCHER, in the America's Cup.

FISCHER, the Gazebo Hotel boss and 1996 Australian Ocean Racing Yachtsman of the Year who recently celebrated his 70th birthday, is again leading the team to Cowes with a brand new BRUCE FARR-designed 49-footer due for launching in Sydney in mid-May.

The second boat in the team is the ILC-40, G Net, which is currently undergoing some modifications in Auckland before being shipped to the UK, where it will be steered by Olympic bronze medallist COLIN BEASHEL for a syndicate headed by Melbourne merchant banker JOHN CALVERT-JONES.

Third team skipper, Sydney advertising agency chief STEVE KULMAR, has chartered an Mumm-36 in the U.S. and will be heading overseas in May to contest the World championship as a lead-up to the Admiral's Cup.
ANCIENT MARINER ALBY BURGIN OFF TO SEA AGAIN

That remarkable yachtsman from Lake Macquarie, 82-year-old ALBY BURGIN, will set another milestone in his long ocean racing career when he sets sail in the 1,200-nautical mile race from Brisbane to Gizo in the Solomons Islands.
Organised for the second year by the Royal Queensland Yacht Squadron, a 21-boat fleet is due to set sail on Saturday, May 17, with BURGIN at the helm of his 52-footer Alstar.
What is even more remarkable is that the old salt will be contesting the two-handed division, with only one other sailor aboard.

Not that short-handed sailing is anything new to ALBY, who has had at least a couple of heart valve operations. Back in 1988 he won the Bicentennial two-handed circumnavigation race, also with Alstar, an aluminium cutter designed by JOE ADAMS.
As he clears the outer fringe of the Great Barrier Reef on course for Gizo, the veteran yachtsman may recall one of his most dramatic sailing experience.
Back in 1972, competing in the Brisbane-to-Gladstone race, the fleet was hit by Cyclone Emily and his then yacht Rival was dismasted in a 360-degree capsize.

ALBY was tossed over board in the 90-knot winds and mountainous seas but as the yacht finally righted itself he found himself right alongside and able to call for help from the rest of the crew down below.
FIDELIS PROVES FASTEST VETERAN

It was a day for the backmarkers in last Sunday's opening day of the Cruising Yacht Club's Winter Series on Sydney Harbour, which also featured the Club's annual Great Veterans Race for yachts which contested Sydney-to-Hobarts before 1965. There was barely a ripple on the Harbour as the front-markers edged to the line for the handicap start, but the breeze began to fill in as the bigger and faster boats got their starting signals.

The Great Veterans Race drew 15 starters with the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron member NIGEL STOKE getting the gun with Fidelis, the former New Zealander flyer which took line honours in the 1966 Hobart race.

Runner-up was Lolita, skippered by solicitor and CYCA stalwart NICK CASSIM, third going to another former Sydney-to-Hobart line honours winner, Margaret Rintoul (1950 and 1951), now owned by city financial adviser BRUCE GOULD.
Waterfront identity, 72-year-old "BOY" MESSENGER, showed he had lost none of his skill by helming MAURIE EVANS' Malohi into fourth place.
Malohi was SYD FISCHER'S first ocean racing yacht which he sailed into fourth place in the Sydney-to-Hobart 35 years ago, under the guidance of MESSENGER as his sailing master.

A record opening day fleet of 155 yachts competed last Sunday with solicitor MARTIN JAMES steering his Farr-65, Infinity III, to victory in Division A by a comfortable margin from Dulux Innkeeper and Assassin.
WORLD GRAND PRIX FOR OLYMPIC 49er

Australian-based Grand Prix Sailing International has been appointed by the International 49er class association to organise an annual "World" 49er Grand Prix series for the new Olympic high-performance dinghy.

Headed by BILL McCARTNEY, best known for his highly successful marketing of the 18-footer Grand Prix circuit in Australia and overseas, Grand Prix Sailing International will conduct six regattas in Europe, the United States and Australia between early June and late November.

Approval by the International Sailing Federation to use the word "World" is pending, but the circuit is expected to attract many of the world's best skiff and dinghy sailors looking towards the Sydney 2000 Olympics.
The grand prix regattas in Australia will be in Adelaide from November 19-16 and in Sydney from November 24-30.
CONNER LAUNCHES WHITBREAD-60

Four-time America's Cup winner and one-time loser DENNIS CONNER must have mixed memories of Newport, Rhode Island, but he was back in his old stamping ground full of smiles yesterday for the christening of his latest yacht, Toshiba.
Conner and one-time rival CHRIS DICKSON will campaign the yacht in this year's Whitbread Round-the-World Race.
Toshiba, which naturally will be equipped with several Toshiba notebook computers with wireless communications capabilities, was designed by BRUCE FARR & Associates.
It is 19.8 metres (65ft) in overall length with a beam of 5.25 metres (17.23ft) and a displacement of 13,500 kg (29,700lb).
Sail area upwind is 200 sq metres (2,154 sq ft) but downwind she will carry a massive 417 sq metres (4,400 sq ft) of sail.

While CONNER and DICKSON have been named as co-skippers, it is expected the New Zealander will skipper on most of the legs of the 32,000 nautical mile race. Navigator will be Australian ANDREW CAPE, who navigated the maxi yachts Sayonara and Morning Glory to victory in the last two Telstra Sydney-to-Hobart races.
*Peter Campbell is editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
